who: Seneca · Letters 71, tr. R. M. Gummere, 1920
quote: There remains much more of the road than we have put behind us; but the greater part of progress is the desire to progress.
meaning: Wanting to grow is most of growing.

who: Confucius and his student Ran Qiu · Analects VI.10, tr. James Legge, 1861
quote: Yen Ch'iu said, ‘It is not that I do not delight in your doctrines, but my strength is insufficient.’ The Master said, ‘Those whose strength is insufficient give over in the middle of the way but now you limit yourself.’
meaning: The weak stop halfway. You stopped before you even started.

who: Dogen · Shobogenzo Zuimonki 2-14, tr. Shohaku Okumura, 1988
quote: It depends only on whether one's aspiration is firmly determined or not. A person who arouses true aspiration and studies as hard as his capacity allows will not fail to attain (the Way).
meaning: Talent is not the key. A firm wish to learn, plus steady effort, gets you there.

who: Helen Keller · The Story of My Life, 1903
quote: ...every one who wishes to gain true knowledge must climb the Hill Difficulty alone... I slip back many times, I fall, I stand still... I trudge on, I gain a little, I feel encouraged, I get more eager and climb higher...
meaning: Learning is a steep hill. You slip and fall, but you keep climbing.

who: The Buddha, about his first teacher · Majjhima Nikaya 26, tr. Bhikkhu Sujato, 2018
quote: It's not just Alara Kalama who has faith, energy, mindfulness, immersion, and wisdom; I too have these things. Why don't I make an effort to realize the same teaching...?
meaning: My teacher has faith and effort. So do I. Why not work and learn it too?

who: Plutarch · On Listening to Lectures 18, tr. F. C. Babbitt, 1927
quote: For the mind does not require filling like a bottle, but rather, like wood, it only requires kindling to create in it an impulse to think independently and an ardent desire for the truth.
meaning: Your mind is not a bottle to fill. It is wood to light.

who: Jane Goodall, on her mother's advice · Science Friday interview, 2002
quote: ...if you really want something, you work hard, you take advantage of opportunity, and you never give up.
meaning: Really want it? Work hard, use every chance, and never give up.

who: Hwang Sang and his teacher Jeong Yak-yong · Imsul-gi, 1862, tr. from Korean
quote: In 1802 Hwang Sang, 15, told his teacher he had three faults: dull, blocked and slow. The answer: ‘The way to dig in? Diligence. To break through? Diligence. To polish? Diligence.’ He kept it for sixty years.
meaning: Think you are too slow to learn? The answer is the same three times: keep working.

who: Russian proverb · V. I. Dal's collection, 1862
quote: Live a lifetime, learn a lifetime.
meaning: Keep learning for as long as you live.

who: K. Pattabhi Jois · as told by Eddie Stern, foreword to Yoga Mala, 2010
quote: In 1930 the young Pattabhi Jois left for Mysore ‘with two rupees in his pocket’ to study Sanskrit. ‘For one or two years he begged for food and slept in the dormitory room of a friend.’ There he found his teacher again.
meaning: Almost no money and no room of his own. He kept learning anyway.
